ghs.en: Nanaka was right next to me.

rows.jp: 忽然と立ち現れたような……。

ghs.en: As if manifested all of a sudden...

ghs.assessment: お元気 is the ordinary greeting 'How are you?' The bare prepositional fragment is not functional English dialogue here.

rows.jp: 「そんなことより、あの祠って―――」

ghs.assessment: 祠 is a small shrine. The English leaves the common noun as an unexplained romanized Japanese word instead of translating it.

rows.jp: 「楽しいって、言えるなら、いいじゃん」
rows.en: “If you can say you’re having fun, that’s good enough.”

ghs.en: Nanaka: "You said fun, and if you can say that, 's all right."
ghs.assessment: The Japanese says that it is good if he can call the experience fun. The English first asserts that he already said the isolated word 'fun,' contradicting the following denial.

highlights.text: You said fun, and if you can say that

rows.jp: つうか会話に脈絡ないんですけど。
rows.en: Also, this conversation has no continuity.

ghs.en: There is no chain of logical connection going through this conversation, however,
ghs.assessment: The Japanese colloquially says that the conversation has no logical continuity. The English expands this into an awkward literal chain running through it.

highlights.text: no chain of logical connection going through this conversation

rows.jp: なんなんだこの唐突感動イベントは……。
rows.en: What is this sudden tearjerker event...?

ghs.en: what is even with this sudden Emotionally Moving Event...
ghs.assessment: The Japanese asks what this sudden touching scene is. The English question lacks a grammatical predicate and gratuitously capitalizes its descriptive phrase.

highlights.text: what is even with this sudden Emotionally Moving Event

rows.jp: しかし、それはそれとして。

ghs.en: Anyway, be that as it may.

rows.jp: あいまいな胸の柔らかさ。
rows.en: The indistinct softness of her chest.

ghs.en: The ambiguous softness of a breast.

rows.jp: 不思議と、猥雑なものは感じない。
rows.en: Strangely, it didn’t feel the least bit obscene.

ghs.en: Inexplicably, I feel nothing out of order.
ghs.assessment: 猥雑 specifically means something lewd, vulgar, or sexually sordid. The English erases that dimension and substitutes the vague idea of disorder.

rows.jp: 抱かれた時の感覚が、曜子ちゃんとは違った。
rows.en: Being held by her felt different from being held by Yoko.

ghs.en: The feeling at the moment of embrace was so different from Youko-chan's.

rows.jp: 「その言葉は、嬉しいんだ。すごく」
rows.en: “Hearing you say that makes me happy. So happy.”

ghs.en: Nanaka: "Those words... they make me happy. Really."

rows.jp: 「強くならないと生きる資格がないわけじゃないから」
rows.en: “You don’t have to become strong to deserve to live.”

ghs.en: Nanaka: "Because never becoming strong is not a disqualification from living."
ghs.assessment: The Japanese says that one need not become strong in order to deserve to live. 'Never becoming strong' adds permanent future failure and the nominal construction is an awkward calque.

highlights.text: never becoming strong is not a disqualification from living

rows.en: “You haven't heard a word I've said.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Listen to what you're being told!"
ghs.assessment: 聞いちゃいねぇ means that Taichi was not listening or did not ask for the speech. The English instead orders Nanaka to listen.

highlights.text: Listen to what you're being told!

rows.jp: わけがわからなかった。
rows.en: I had no idea what was going on.

ghs.en: I didn't understand any of this.

rows.jp: 「胸の感触はすごくよかった」

ghs.en: Taichi: "I'm really glad to have experienced the tactile feeling of your chest."

rows.jp: 「ただわけはわからなかった」
rows.en: “I just had no idea what was going on.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "It's just that I didn't get this at all."

ghs.assessment: Nanaka says that she was mistaken or got something wrong. 'Mistook you' specifically claims that she confused Taichi's identity with another person's.
Taichi asks what she mistook him for. 'For what?' instead asks the purpose or reason.

rows.jp: 「理解できるように説明して」

ghs.en: Taichi: "Explain in ways I can understand."
ghs.assessment: The line asks for a single intelligible manner of explanation; the English plural produces a malformed collocation.

rows.jp: 「キミってアンテナ設営の方、着手したみたいだけど、進捗はどう？」
rows.en: “Seems like you've started setting up the antenna. How's it going?”

ghs.en: Nanaka: "Say you, it looks like you're setting out on helping the construction on that antenna, but how's progress?"
ghs.assessment: The Japanese says that he seems to have begun the antenna installation and asks how it is progressing. The English adds 'helping,' uses a malformed 'setting out on ... construction,' and omits the article before 'progress.'

highlights.text: Nanaka: "Say you, it looks like you're setting out on helping the construction on that antenna, but how's progress?"

rows.jp: 「わかるように話そう。まず……まずだ」
rows.en: “Let's try this in words I can understand. First... first of all.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Let's talk so that I can understand. First... first up is..."

rows.jp: 「そうだな、いろいろあるんだが」
rows.en: “Well, there are all kinds of things...”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Of course, there's a lots and a lots, but..."
ghs.assessment: The Japanese says simply that there are various things. The English invents repetition and twice combines the singular article with a plural noun.

highlights.text: there's a lots and a lots

rows.jp: 「じゃあ一個だけ質問に答えてあげる。どんなことでも答えるよ？」
rows.en: “Then I'll answer one question. Ask me anything.”

ghs.en: Nanaka: "Theeen one single solitary question I'll give you an answer to. Ask me anything and I'll answer, OK?"

rows.jp: 「今日は白。でもちょっとかわいいの。ブラとおそろいのやつなんだ」
rows.en: “White today. A cute pair, though. They match my bra.”

ghs.en: Nanaka: "Today they're white. But they're reeeally cute tho. They totally match the bra!"
ghs.assessment: The Japanese says that the underwear is somewhat cute and matches the bra. The English raises 'somewhat' to 'really' and adds emphatic slang to both clauses.

rows.jp: 少女の下着に思いを馳せた。
rows.en: My mind wanders to a young girl's underwear.

ghs.en: I reflect nostalgically on the girl's underwear.
ghs.assessment: 思いを馳せる means letting one's thoughts dwell on something. The English adds nostalgia, which the Japanese does not state.

rows.jp: 「じゃ質問はこれで打ち切ります」
rows.en: “And that's the end of question time.”

ghs.en: Nanaka: "Well, the questioning round is with this brought to a close."
ghs.assessment: The Japanese straightforwardly closes the questions. The English follows Japanese constituent order into an ungrammatical passive construction.

highlights.text: the questioning round is with this brought to a close

rows.jp: 「うおー、しまったー、世界の謎がー！」
rows.en: “Aargh, I blew it! The mysteries of the world!”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Woooooh, dammiiiit, what about the mystery of this wooorld!!!"

rows.jp: 反射的に質問してしまったぁ！

ghs.en: I fired off a question by refleeex!

rows.jp: 腕でバッテンを作る七香。
rows.en: Nanaka crosses her arms into an X.

ghs.en: Nanaka crosses her arm into a X, making the Batten mark of denial and failure.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese says that Nanaka makes an X with her arms. The English retains batten as an unexplained capitalized Japanese word and invents an explanatory doctrine of denial and failure.

highlights.text: the Batten mark of denial and failure

ghs.assessment: The Japanese says only that there will be another chance. The English appends an unsupported fragment.

rows.jp: 「次って、俺もうこの会話忘れちゃってんじゃん」
rows.en: “Next? I'll have forgotten this whole conversation by then.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Next? But I'll have forgotten this conversation by then, won't I."

rows.jp: 「気づくさ。けど気づいただけで、どうしてこんなことになったとか、人類どうなったとか、わかんないことだらけだ」
rows.en: “Of course I noticed. But that's all. I still don't know why this happened or what happened to humanity or any of the rest.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Noticed I did. But even noticing that I'm still full of stuff I dun'no, like, say, why has this all ended up like this, or what happened to humanity."

rows.jp: 「どうしてこうなったか、なんてあたしにもわからんよ」
rows.en: “I don't know why this happened, either.”

ghs.en: Nanaka: "As to why this all ended up like this, I don't understand it myself either."

rows.jp: 小首を傾けて、可愛らしく問いかける。
rows.en: I cock my head and ask cutely.

ghs.en: Tilting my neck, I ask the question in an adorable way.
ghs.assessment: 小首を傾ける is a slight, often cute tilt of the head. The English substitutes the neck as the body part being tilted.

rows.jp: 小首を傾けて、可愛らしく返された。
rows.en: She cocks her head and answers cutely.

ghs.en: Tilting her neck, she answered the question in an adorable way.
ghs.assessment: 小首を傾ける describes a slight tilt of the head, not tilting the neck itself.

rows.jp: 「まあ……こうなったとしか言えない」
rows.en: “Well... all I can say is that it happened.”

ghs.en: Nanaka: "Well... besides that it did get like this I can't say."
ghs.assessment: Nanaka says that she can only say this is how things turned out. The English reverses the limiting construction into an ungrammatical 'besides' clause.

highlights.text: besides that it did get like this I can't say

rows.jp: 「理由を考えようにも、ぜーんぜんわかりまっせーん」
rows.en: “As for why, I have nooo ideaaa.”

ghs.en: Nanaka: "I think about the reason but still I don't understand aaaanything at aaall."
ghs.assessment: 理由を考えようにも means 'even if I try to think of the reason.' The English states an ongoing successful act of thinking and loses the concessive relation.

highlights.text: I think about the reason but still

rows.jp: 「花も恥じらう女学生に何を期待しておるのかね」
rows.en: “What do you expect of a schoolgirl in the first bloom of youth?”

ghs.en: Nanaka: "What could you expect from a schoolgirl whose beauty would make even flowers blush!"

rows.jp: 「だいたいさあ、おかしいんだよ！」

ghs.en: Taichi: "Well, first of all, that's kinda weird innit!"

ghs.assessment: The Japanese asks 'What is?' only because the preceding adjective is recoverable in Japanese. English requires that predicate to be supplied, such as 'What is weird?'

rows.jp: 「普通、キミみたいな役割はもっと大人しい電波っぽい娘がやるものだろ！」
rows.en: “A role like yours is supposed to go to a quieter, spacey girl!”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Normally, roles like yours would be assigned to a much more docile Denpa-emitter of a crazy girl, definitely."
ghs.assessment: The Japanese says the role normally belongs to a quieter, denpa-like girl. The English invents an emitter, explicitly declares her crazy, and adds 'definitely.'

highlights.text: a much more docile Denpa-emitter of a crazy girl, definitely

rows.jp: 「キミは勝ち気な幼なじみっぽいんだから、造形にふさわしく物語からの要請事項に従って俺の隣にでも住んで毎朝起こしに来いよ！」
rows.en: “You look like the strong-willed childhood-friend type, so obey the demands of the story, move in next door, and come wake me up every morning!”

ghs.en: Taichi: "You're the unyielding childhood friend type, therefore, obey the matters demanded from stories suitable to be molds and live next door to me and come wake me up every day!"
ghs.assessment: The Japanese invokes story conventions appropriate to Nanaka's character design. The English turns the design into things suitable to be molds and produces an unintelligible demand phrase.

highlights.text: the matters demanded from stories suitable to be molds

rows.en: I point a finger at her.

ghs.en: I thrust a finger at her.

ghs.assessment: The source uses a rough second-person form, but the English creates an ungrammatical inversion and a generic eye-dialect 'ya.'

rows.jp: 「ただ配置を変えれば特別なことをしてるとでも思ったか、低脳短絡が」
rows.en: “You think rearranging the cast is enough to make you special, you shallow-minded moron?”

ghs.en: Taichi: "If you think you're doing something special just by making changes from the normal arrangements, you're a short-cutting imbecile!"

rows.jp: 「そーいうのを表層的な思考と言うんだ」

ghs.en: Taichi: "For that may certainly be said to be a surface-level reasoning!"
ghs.assessment: Nanaka says, 'That's what you call superficial thinking.' The English uses an ungoverned 'for,' an unnecessary passive, and a count noun where English requires 'reasoning' as a mass noun.

highlights.text: For that may certainly be said to be a surface-level reasoning!

rows.jp: 「変わったことがしたければ、根底からやってみろ。今まで誰もしたことがないようなやつをだ！」
rows.en: “If you want to do something different, do it from the roots up. Something no one has ever done before!”

ghs.en: Taichi: "If you wanna make a change, try doing it from the grounds up. Do something that no one has ever done up until now!"
ghs.assessment: 根底から corresponds to the fixed English expression 'from the ground up,' with singular 'ground.'

ghs.en: Nanaka: "All those words riiight back at ya."

rows.jp: 「俺は表層的なアンチテーゼにばかり目を奪われた低脳短絡ですーっ！！」
rows.en: “I'm a shallow-minded moron dazzled by nothing but surface-level antitheses!”

ghs.en: Taichi: "I am a short-cutting imbecile who is exclusively enthralled by superficial antithesiiiis!!!"
ghs.assessment: 低脳短絡 insults a stupid, simplistic thinker. 'Short-cutting' instead describes someone who takes practical shortcuts and is not an idiomatic personal epithet.

ghs.en: Nanaka: "Cry not, cry not little one."
ghs.assessment: 若者 addresses him as a young man or youth, not as a small child.

rows.jp: 「……ま、こうなったら次の機会に同じ質問をしてくれることを祈るのみだな」
rows.en: “...Well, all I can do now is hope I ask the same question next time.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "...well, if it turns like this, I pray that the next time we meet I'll ask just the same question."

rows.jp: 「コレがまた意外と違うんだなぁ」
rows.en: “The funny thing is, that’s different too.”

ghs.en: Nanaka: "This one's already unexpectedly different, yes."
ghs.assessment: Nanaka says, roughly, 'Surprisingly, that actually varies.' The English's 'already' and 'this one' do not identify the varying behavior and the sentence is not idiomatic.

highlights.text: This one's already unexpectedly different, yes.

rows.jp: 「他の人たちは日曜夜の時点でもう気持ちが決まってるから、毎回似たような行動取るんだけどさ」
rows.en: “Everyone else has made up their minds by Sunday night, so they do pretty much the same thing each time.”

ghs.en: Nanaka: "The other guys, their emotions are already decided on that point on Sunday night, so they take similar actions every time."
ghs.assessment: The Japanese says that the others have made up their minds by Sunday night. The English literalizes feelings as decided objects and mistranslates the time boundary as a point on Sunday.

highlights.text: their emotions are already decided on that point on Sunday night

rows.en: “But you're pretty different every time, Taichi.”

ghs.en: Nanaka: "But you, Taichi, you're pretty different every time."

rows.jp: 「……ことを重大に受け止めてないというか」
rows.en: “...It's like you don't take all this that seriously.”

ghs.en: Nanaka: "...you never take things seriously, more like."

ghs.assessment: うーん marks hesitation or thought, like 'hmm.' 'Nah' communicates rejection or disagreement.

rows.jp: 俺自身のことを考えると、他人は少ない方がいい。
rows.en: When I consider my own nature, the fewer other people, the better.

ghs.en: When I think about myself, I'm fine with there being few other people.

rows.jp: だから今の状況は、そう悪くないと思ってる。
rows.en: That's why I don't think the current situation is so bad.

ghs.en: Therefore I don't think the way things are right now are all that bad.
ghs.assessment: The head of the subject is singular 'way,' so the English predicate must be 'is.'

highlights.text: the way things are right now are

rows.jp: まったく不安がないといえば嘘になるが……。
rows.en: I'd be lying if I said I wasn't worried at all, but...

ghs.en: If I said there was no anxiety at all that'd be lying, but...

rows.en: At least, from the conversation we just had.

ghs.en: For the present, that is the conversation.

rows.jp: 自転車でウイリーを試みている七香を見やる。
rows.en: I glance at Nanaka, who's attempting a wheelie on her bike.

ghs.en: I stare at Nanaka trying out a wheelie on her bicycle.

rows.jp: この人……記憶リセットかかってないってこと。
rows.en: So this means... her memory isn't being reset.

ghs.en: This person here... does not have her memories reset.

ghs.assessment: Nanaka proposes that they keep what was said or honor the agreement. The English makes it a unilateral claim about whatever she says and does.

rows.jp: 「別に隠しているわけではないんだけど……ね」
rows.en: “It's not that I'm trying to hide anything from you... exactly.”

ghs.en: Nanaka: "It's not that I'm hiding something or the likes tho... 'K."

rows.jp: 「太一が追いつめられるような気がして」
rows.en: “I feel like it would back you into a corner.”

ghs.en: Nanaka: "There's this feeling like it will drive you into a corner, Taichi."

rows.jp: 快活だった表情が、危惧を形作る。
rows.en: Her buoyant expression tightens into worry.

ghs.en: The expression on her face that was cheerful now takes the shape of apprehension.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese says her formerly cheerful expression becomes one of concern. The English literalizes the emotion as a shape taken by the face.
そう acknowledges what she has said, like 'I see.' 'Well' instead signals hesitation or transition.

rows.en: Well, a promise is a promise.

rows.jp: 湿っぽくなっちゃいました。

rows.en: I decide to lighten the mood.

ghs.en: I decided to soften this down.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese says that Taichi decides to lighten the mood. 'Soften this down' is not the English idiom for that action.

rows.jp: 「あの……質問じゃないんだけど、さっきの下着の件さぁ」
rows.en: “Um... not a question, but about that underwear from before...”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Uhm... it's not a question, but, about that underwear thing from before..."

rows.jp: 「ブラはフロントホックをつけて欲しいんですけど」
rows.en: “I'd like you to wear a front-clasp bra.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "I would sure like for the bra to be front hook."
ghs.assessment: The Japanese requests a front-hook bra. English requires the compound adjective 'front-hooked' or the noun phrase 'a front-hook bra.'

highlights.text: the bra to be front hook

rows.jp: 七香は訝しげに眉をよじった。
rows.en: Nanaka knits her brows in puzzlement.

rows.jp: 「フロントホックって……この花も恥じらう女学生である七香さんに？」
rows.en: “A front clasp... for Nanaka, a schoolgirl in the first bloom of youth?”

ghs.en: Nanaka: "Front hook bra you say... on Nanaka-san, this schoolgirl whose beauty would make even flowers blush?"

rows.jp: 「こう、女の子と初夜った時にさ、ブラを外すじゃないですか」%N※初夜る＝太一語。初Ｈのこと。
rows.en: “When you first-night with a girl, you take off her bra, right?”%N※“To first-night” is Taichi-speak for having sex for the first time.

rows.jp: 「フロントホックであれば、こう谷間に差し入れた指で小粋にフィンガースナップを奏でつつホックを外したその瞬間、いましめから解放されたたわわな母なる双丘がたわわんと」
rows.en: “With a front clasp, you can slip your fingers into the cleavage and undo the clasp with a jaunty snap—and at that very instant, the bountiful maternal twin peaks, freed from their bonds, bounti-bounce...”

ghs.en: Taichi: "If a front hook is present, then fingers can be inserted in the cleavage's ravine and sound out a stylish fingersnap as they undo the hook, and on that very instant, the boioingy twin hills of a mother shall be released from bondage and boioioingly..."

rows.jp: 「自分で思っているほど、たいしたギャグじゃない」
rows.en: “It's not as great a joke as you think.”

ghs.en: Nanaka: "That's not as funny a joke as you think it is inside yourself."
ghs.assessment: 自分で思っているほど means 'as funny as you think it is.' The English adds a literal and redundant interior location.

rows.jp: 「つ……つまりその、揺れる様を鑑賞することかできるから、です！」
rows.en: “I-I mean, because then I can admire the way they bounce!”

ghs.en: Taichi: "In-... in other words, because it allows the artistic appreciation of the act of swaying, indeed!"

rows.jp: そんな馬鹿なことを話していると。
rows.en: While we're talking about such idiotic things.

ghs.en: And while we were talking about these stupid little things,

rows.en: Before long, we reach my house.

ghs.en: we ended up at my house.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese says that they soon reach his house. 'Ended up' implies an unintended destination not present in the source.

rows.jp: どこに帰っているんだろう、七香は。
rows.en: Where does Nanaka go home to?

ghs.en: where would Nanaka even go home to?
ghs.assessment: Taichi wonders where she habitually goes home. The conditional 'would go' instead frames a hypothetical destination.

highlights.text: where would Nanaka even go home to?

rows.jp: 頭だけ巡らせて、背後を視野におさめた。
rows.en: I turn just my head and take in the view behind me.

ghs.en: I turned the head alone, laying the rear in my field of vision.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese says that he turns only his head and brings the space behind him into view. The English uses 'rear' as an object and describes laying it somewhere.

highlights.text: laying the rear in my field of vision

rows.en: Nanaka is at the top of the hill.

ghs.en: Nanaka was on top of the hill.

rows.jp: 瞬時に移動したような。
rows.en: As if she'd moved there in an instant.

ghs.en: as if she had moved in an instant.

rows.jp: 離れているにもかかわらず、声は冴え冴えと耳に届いた。
rows.en: Despite the distance, her voice reaches me, crystal clear.

ghs.en: Her voice carried clear and crisp in spite of being so distant, as if it had fangs that bit into my ears.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese says only that her voice reaches him with striking clarity despite the distance. The fangs and biting are invented imagery.

highlights.text: as if it had fangs that bit into my ears

ghs.en: I lose my presence of mind.

rows.jp: 自転車の脇に立ち、片手を高々とあげる。空を支えて、笑顔。
rows.en: Standing beside her bike, one hand raised high. Holding up the sky, smiling.

ghs.en: Standing at the side of her bicycle, raising one hand high and higher. Holding up the sky. Smiling.

ghs.assessment: 振り返した means that Taichi waves back. 'Asserted' is an unrelated speech-act verb.

rows.jp: 走り出すと、少女の姿は坂の窪みを滑り降りて見えなくなる。
rows.en: She sets off, and the girl glides down into a hollow in the hill, disappearing from view.

ghs.en: Setting out to ride, the figure of the girl begins to descend into the valley between hills, and vanishes from sight.

rows.jp: いくら待っても、向こう側の斜面をよじのぼる姿を見ることはできなかった―――
rows.en: No matter how long I wait, I never see her climb the slope on the other side—

ghs.en: I never could see the figure of her climbing up on the slope on the opposite side, however long I waited---
